page.title: Best Silent Hall Effect Keyboard (2026): Quiet Magnetic Switches Compared
page.desc: Few hall effect keyboards ship with silent magnetic switches. We compare the Gamakay TK75HE V2, NS75 and TK75 TMR, plus the Keychron K2 HE for Mac and Wooting for DIY.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best silent hall effect keyboard is the Gamakay TK75HE V2 ({buy:gamakay-tk75he-v2}): it ships with Phoenix V3 silent magnetic switches, works by cable, 2.4 GHz or Bluetooth, and is rated for 8,000 Hz polling with rapid trigger. Very few prebuilt boards ship with silent magnetic switches; HLPlanet calls Gamakay's “essentially the only mainstream” option.

Check this first: it is a Windows keyboard. On a Mac, Gamakay's driver never detected it in AppleInsider’s test (2.5 out of 5), so you could not tune actuation. Mac owners should look at the Keychron K2 HE, which has Mac keycaps and a web app that supports macOS. Its stock switches are not silent.

How quiet is it? AppleInsider heard a soft “thunk” rather than a clack. HLPlanet calls the Phoenix V3 “really quiet” and says it avoids the mushy bottom-out of many silent switches. The keys with stabilizers (space, shift, backspace) are the loudest part. On Gamakay's silent mechanical TK75 V2, Notebookcheck heard them tick.

Want a lower price and a volume knob? The {buy:gamakay-ns75} uses the same Phoenix V3 switch option but has had little independent testing. Use it wireless all day? The {buy:gamakay-tk75-tmr} adds an 8,000 mAh battery and also takes silent mechanical switches.

page.after:
What owners and reviewers complain about

  • Software (6 of the 6 reviews we read). Gamakay's driver is called confusing or half-baked, is English only, and in AppleInsider's test did not work on a Mac at all.
  • Plastic build (3 reviews). PC Gamer, AppleInsider and HLPlanet all call the case cheap. AppleInsider says it picks up finger oil.
  • The dongle falls out (2 reviews). With the rear feet open, the 2.4 GHz receiver drops out of its slot. Keep it plugged into the PC instead.
  • Phantom key releases (2 sources). Rapid trigger set below about 0.3 mm can misfire on the TK75 TMR. HLPlanet's fix is 0.4 mm, and Gamakay suggests a 0.3 mm dead zone.
  • Silent switches don't fit every board (4 sources). Keychron's HE boards take only their own Gateron or Keychron magnetic switches, and DrunkDeer boards take only Raesha switches. Phoenix V3 fits open, N-pole-down boards such as the Wooting 60HE.
  • Slow, costly returns. Shipping takes about 10-15 days from Gamakay's US warehouse. Returns are within 14 days at your cost, and opened working items can carry a 35% restocking fee.

Which one by need

  • Quiet gaming and typing in a shared room, under $100: Gamakay TK75HE V2. It has the most independent reviews of any board that ships with silent magnetic switches.
  • Lowest price, or you want a knob: Gamakay NS75 with the Phoenix V3 option. It has the same switch but fewer reviews.
  • All-day wireless, or silent mechanical keys too: Gamakay TK75 TMR. It has an 8,000 mAh battery and runs 8,000 Hz over 2.4 GHz.
  • Mac: Keychron K2 HE. It has Mac keycaps and macOS-friendly software, but its stock switches are not silent.
  • Best software, wired, and you will swap switches: a Wooting board fitted with Gateron Magnetic Jade Silent switches. Divinikey sells them at $14.22 for 18 (seen 2026-11-11), so a 75% board needs about five packs.

Not recommended

  • The original TK75HE (V1). Gamakay says its V1 switches work only in that board, and it can't take other brands' magnetic switches. Buy the V2.
  • Buying silent magnetic switches for a Keychron or DrunkDeer HE board. They won't fit those boards' switch systems.
